transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Since my husband passed, it feels like everything inside me just shut down, and I can’t make myself do the things I used to care about. I just don't have the strength to keep up with my life anymore, and everything feels so heavy.
I am so sorry for your loss. Could you tell me how long ago your husband passed away, and how long you have been experiencing these feelings?

Thank you, doctor... it's been hard, he passed away about three years ago. These numb, shut-down feelings started creeping in during that first year after he died, and it has stayed about the same for a little over two years now.
During these past two years, have you had any periods lasting two months or longer where you felt like your usual self and your mood improved?
No, I haven't had any times like that at all. This numb, shut-down feeling has just been constant, staying about the same the whole two years without any breaks or feeling like my old self again.
Along with this heavy and numb feeling, have you noticed any changes in your sleeping habits or your appetite over these past two years?
I haven't really noticed or paid much attention to my sleep or my appetite. I've just been so focused on trying to get through each day that I don't think about those things much.
Over these past two years, have you also been struggling with feelings of hopelessness, or felt like your self-esteem has been very low?
I haven't really felt hopeless or had low self-esteem, no. It's more that I just feel completely numb, empty, and shut down inside.
Over these past two years, have you found it difficult to concentrate, focus on daily tasks, or make decisions?

Yes, focusing on anything has been incredibly hard these past two years. I often just sit staring at the TV without registering what's playing, and simple tasks like opening mail, bathing, or making a meal feel completely overwhelming. I just can't bring myself to do any of it anymore.
Along with feeling heavy and shut down, have you also felt constantly tired, fatigued, or lacking in energy over these past two years?

Yes, I feel completely drained of energy, but it is more like my inner drive has been totally switched off. I just don't have the strength or the will to get up and do anything anymore, so I just sit there.
During these past two years, have you experienced any thoughts of death, wishing you could slip away, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wishing to die. Even though I feel completely empty and shut down inside, I don't want to do any harm to myself.
Have you been experiencing any strong feelings of guilt, or do you find yourself blaming yourself for things that are out of your control?
No, I don't really feel guilty or blame myself for anything. It's just that since my husband passed, I feel completely empty, numb, and shut down inside.
To help me understand the timing better, did these feelings of being shut down and numb start within the first three months after your husband passed away?
No, they didn't start right away in those first three months. It was more of a slow, creeping change that gradually built up over that first year after he passed away.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent depressed (numb and empty) mood lasting continuously for over two years, with no symptom-free periods of two months or longer. She meets the diagnostic criteria for Dysthymia (F34.1) by exhibiting two of the required secondary symptoms: low energy/fatigue and poor concentration/difficulty making decisions. Although her symptoms followed the death of her husband three years ago, they did not begin within the first three months of bereavement, and their chronic, unremitting nature over two years supports a diagnosis of dysthymia rather than an acute adjustment disorder.
